si4_title: Patterns of connectome variability in autism across five functional activation tasks: findings from the LEAP project

dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The EU-AIMS/AIMS-2-TRIALS multisite Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) dataset.
dc1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The  dataset  from  the  EU-AIMS/AIMS2TRIALS  LEAP project was used for the current analyses-a large multicenter European project with an aim to identify biomarkers

answer.LEAP: normative training and validation for the 5 task-based normative models, and patient for clinical research (atypicality mapping and brain-behavior relationship analysis)

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Typically developing (TD) controls from LEAP were used to build and validate normative models for each task. The autism group from LEAP was used for mapping individual atypicalities and analyzing brain-behavior relationships.
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Normative modelling was used to map atypicality of features on an individual basis with respect to their distribution in neurotypical control participants. ... The inclusion of data for analyses from the following participants:  282  participants  with  autism ... and  221 typically  developing  controls
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Looden2022.pdf.md: Abstract / Methods; Materials and methods / Sample

dc3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norma.detail: Total TD participants included in the study was 221, but task-specific counts were not explicitly reported (NR) although characterizations of subsamples were provided. Since the study states all analyses were based on the pool of 282 ASD and 221 TD, the overall-phase N is provided as 221.
dc3_healthy_control_number_of_each_norma.supporting_text: 221 typically  developing  controls ... Not every participant was included in each analysis, for the reason that not all participants completed all fMRI scan sessions.
